holidays.name: Cream Cheese Brownie Day
holidays.description: A day for chocolate lovers to celebrate the swirled, tangy-meets-fudgy dessert that puts cream cheese and brownie batter in the same pan. Bake a batch, marbled top and all, and call it a holiday.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a fixture on February food-holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Cream cheese was invented in 1872 in New York, when dairyman William Lawrence was trying to copy a French cheese and ended up with something creamier.

holidays.name: Plimsoll Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the Plimsoll line, the mark on a ship's hull that shows how heavily it can be loaded before it becomes unsafe. It honors the humble stripe that has kept countless sailors from sinking.
holidays.origin: The day is tied to British politician Samuel Plimsoll, who campaigned for ship safety in the 19th century. His efforts led to the Merchant Shipping Act of 1876, which made load lines mandatory.
holidays.funFact: Plimsoll was so well known that people nicknamed him 'the sailors' friend,' and the rubber-soled shoes called plimsolls are said to be named after the line. The shoe's rubber band resembled the line on a hull.

holidays.name: Umbrella Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the rain-stopping, sun-blocking, occasionally inside-out gadget that keeps us dry. Grab your brolly and give it a twirl, even if the sky is perfectly clear.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is celebrated each year in the middle of winter, when umbrellas get plenty of use.
holidays.funFact: Umbrellas were first used as shade from the sun, and ancient Chinese, Egyptian and Assyrian cultures all used them. Waterproofing them for rain came later.
